parsed.why: No criminalisation; X passport/ID markers, bathroom guidance, self-declaration custody placement with consulted preference, enforced hate-crime and anti-discrimination rulings. Offset by documented ongoing violence, discrimination, and one-state male-unit prison practice.

Self-declaration recognition, the region's broadest hate-crime statute covering gender identity, visible Pride scenes, 61% public support. Negatives are mostly resident-facing (care waits, no nonbinary marker, rising prejudice), leaving little visitor-facing exposure.

Nationwide criminalisation of same-sex conduct under military rule, with foreigners to be deported, promotion banned, no gender recognition, no anti-violence mechanism, no LGBT organisations. No prosecutions yet, but structural hostility and witch-hunt fear dominate.

Decriminalisation via constitutional challenge and an equality ruling help, but employment law excludes gender identity, officials question LGBT legitimacy, fundamentalist rhetoric spreads, and a violent attack produced no jail time — thin trans-specific recourse.

Transition itself criminalised at 5-10 years with no suspension, plus 10-20 years for organisations; a coordinated state witch-hunt has produced dozens of arrests and judges sanctioned for acquittals. State-directed targeting with no protections.
